newsitem.title: BELGIUM: FOCUS-EU bans aid to Hoffmann-Laroche.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-EU bans aid to Hoffmann-Laroche.

text.p: The European Commission, determined to clamp down on subsidies to the manufacturing industry, told Germany on Wednesday to recover 600 million marks ($354 million) it granted machinery firm Sket and Austria not to pay 340 million schillings ($28.5 million) to Hoffmann-Laroche.

It said the money proposed to help Hoffmann-Laroche, a subsidiary of Swiss drugs giant Roche Holding AG, develop a new anti-obesity drug called Orlistat was not justified under EU rules on aid to research and development.

The Commission argued that at the time the Austrian authories sought permission to grant the aid the drug was already in its trial phase and that Hoffmann-Laroche would have carried on the project with or without public subsidies.
"The incentive effect of the proposed aid - an inducement for the company to carry out research which it would not otherwise have pursued - is non existent," it said in a statement.
But the Commission found that another 42.8 million schillings in aid to help Hoffmann-Laroche reduce the release of gases or waste into the environment were acceptable.

A Commission spokesman said the Commission had also agreed in principle to ask the German government to recover 600 million marks from bankrupt east German heavy machinery firm Sket granted between 1994 and 1996 in the form of credit waivers, equity loans and guarantees.
The formal decision was delayed one week for technical reasons, he said, also denying earlier press reports that Sket would have to reimburse the double of that amount.

The company, once the main supplier to communist eastern Europe, has received over a billion marks in state aid since German reunification in 1990 but that was unsufficient to ensure its survival. In 1993, the Commission approved a total 327 million marks.
The German authorities will have two months from receiving the Commission's letter to inform it of the measures taken to recover the money.

In a third decision, the Commission gave its assent to a total 500 million marks to help build the Costa I cruise ship and two container ships at Bremer Vulkan's shipyard in Bremen, the spokesman said.
He added that the money had been allowed on the assumption that the Bremer Vulkanwerft yard would be closed down, thus reducing the overall shipbuilding capacity in Germany.
Bremer Vulkan went into receivership last year amid accusations by the Commission that it had siphoned off hundreds of million marks in subsidies intended for its eastern subsidiaries.
The Commission has often criticised Germany for spending huge amounts of public money to rescue large industries in the former east Germany.

A recent report on state aid to the European manufacturing industry between 1992 and 1994 found that Germany alone paid 40 percent of total subsidies of 42.6 billion European currency units ($49 billion) annually. $1 = 1.695 marks $1 = 11.935 shillings $1 = 0.868 ecus -- Brussels newsroom 322 2876841
